# Cameras Decoded

> Cameras Decoded is an interactive training platform that turns mirrorless camera owners into confident operators. Members learn with game-style lessons and daily drills, prove it in the Arena — a daily photo competition — and earn with client tools like galleries and contracts. It serves mirrorless owners at every level: beginners learning their camera (Learn), intermediates sharpening their eye (Play), and working photographers booking clients (Earn). Instruction is led by Cynetis-7, the platform's AI instructor. Free to start; Pro unlocks the full curriculum.

## Start here

- The app: https://camerasdecoded.com
- Field Manual — interactive mirrorless lessons: https://camerasdecoded.com/field-manual.html
- The Arena — daily photo competition: https://camerasdecoded.com/missions.html
- Camera Confidence Guide — the 142-page book ($47): https://camerasdecoded.com/camera-confidence-guide.html
- The Founding 200 — founding member wall: https://camerasdecoded.com/founding-200.html
- Free downloads and the free tier: https://camerasdecoded.com/free.html
- Protocols — the numbered training system: https://camerasdecoded.com/protocols.html

- [What Ten Years With One Subject Can Teach You](https://camerasdecoded.com/blog/ten-years-one-subject.html)
  Ivan McClellan first encountered Black rodeo culture in Oklahoma in 2015. A decade of returning built the relationships behind Eight Seconds: Legacy in Motion, a book of more than 90 previously unpublished photographs.
  In short: Stay with one subject long enough for the pictures to get past the obvious. Photographer Ivan McClellan spent more than a decade with Black rodeo culture, and the result is a book of over 90 previously unpublished photographs that no single visit could have produced.

- [Depth Is Not the Blur](https://camerasdecoded.com/blog/depth-without-wide-aperture.html)
  Max Kent calls a wide aperture the lazy version of depth. His case: soft light from roughly 45 degrees above and to the side, plus a clear foreground, midground, and background, build separation that survives even at f/8.
  In short: Blur is the easiest depth you can buy, which is exactly why it says the least. Photographer Max Kent argues that real depth comes from directional light and layered composition, and his test is simple: shrink a frame to a black-and-white thumbnail, and if the subject still separates, the depth is real.

  In short: Sigma's newest 50mm lens is small, metal, and deliberately imperfect at the corners. The company says it let go of sterile, clinical sharpness on purpose, which is a sign the industry has started selling character again instead of only test-chart numbers.

## About

Cameras Decoded is a Duolingo-style training platform for mirrorless camera owners — interactive lessons (the Field Manual), daily drills and games, a nightly photo competition (the Arena), and client tools for working photographers. The Camera Confidence Guide is its 142-page companion book. The blog covers camera gear, shooting technique, and industry news for mirrorless photographers.
